If you look at the map (Figure 14.26) showing contours within Yosemite National Park in California, you will notice that the streams flow perpendicular to the contours. The streams are following paths of steepest descent so the waters reach lower elevations as quickly as possible. Therefore, the fastest instantaneous rate of change in a stream’s eleva- tion above sea level has a particular direction. In this section, you will see why this direc- tion, called the “downhill” direction, is perpendicular to the contours.
